finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml::the iterate prompt interpolates branch-produced diagnosis text with no data fence, and the review-panel fence it is modelled on is closeable by the untrusted text
evidence: The two code facts are as described. In agent-iterate-ci.yml the "Run Claude Code" prompt splices `${{ steps.diag.outputs.summary }}` with only the line "Structured failure diagnosis from the harness reports:" — no delimiter and no "treat as data" instruction — while agent-review-panel.yml wraps `steps.findings.outputs.summary` in a plain `<panel-findings>` tag with no escaping, so summary text containing the literal closing tag would terminate the fence. The provenance chain is also real: verify-self.mjs's `extractFailureSummary` lifts a line (<=500 chars) straight out of branch-produced lane output, summarize-ci.mjs re-prints it verbatim, and the fix job holds a contents:write App token. What the claim understates is the marginal risk: the same actor who can shape that lane output already controls branch code that this very job checks out, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (postinstall) executes, and an unrestricted-Bash agent runs — and fork events plus the agent/ branch gate mean only base-repo write holders reach it, so the injection channel adds little over the code execution already granted (a risk the design doc explicitly accepts). I could not inspect review-panel.mjs/summary.md generation to confirm how literally lens summaries quote diff text, so the fence-escape half is reasoned rather than verified end to end.
